_about: Curated Earth analog catalog for TwinWorlds. Climate dimensions are NOT stored here: they are computed from NASA POWER climatology (see pipeline/build_data.py). The terrain/geology dimensions below are 0-1 expert estimates from published literature (v0.1) and should be refined with field data. usage = how intensively the site is already used as a space analog (1 = flagship analog, 0 = never used). access = logistics ease (1 = road + airport nearby).

sites.name: Atacama Desert – Yungay
sites.note: Driest non-polar place on Earth; nitrates and perchlorates like Mars soils. NASA rover/life-detection testbed.

sites.name: Haughton Crater – Devon Island
sites.note: 23 km impact crater in polar desert; NASA Haughton-Mars Project.

sites.name: Death Valley
sites.note: Evaporites, alluvial fans, playas; Mars rover and spectroscopy tests.

sites.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
sites.note: Coldest, driest Earth environment; ice-cemented ground like Martian mid-latitudes.

sites.name: Mauna Kea – PISCES ISRU site
sites.note: Basaltic tephra used as lunar regolith simulant; ISRU and robotics tests.

sites.name: Ka'ū Desert – Kīlauea
sites.note: Fresh basalt, acid alteration and lava tubes; NASA BASALT program.

sites.name: Bockfjorden – Svalbard (AMASE)
sites.note: Volcanic carbonates similar to ALH84001 meteorite; Mars instrument trials.

sites.name: Río Tinto
sites.note: Acidic iron/sulfate waters (jarosite) like Meridiani Planum.

sites.name: Timanfaya & La Corona lava tube – Lanzarote
sites.note: ESA PANGAEA / CAVES training ground; basaltic lava tubes.

sites.name: Holuhraun lava field
sites.note: 2014–15 basaltic flood lava with black sand plains; Mars rover tests.

sites.name: Mars Desert Research Station – Hanksville
sites.note: Mars Society habitat; Jurassic sediments, clays and gypsum.

sites.name: Craters of the Moon
sites.note: Basaltic lava flows and tubes; Apollo 14 astronaut training; NASA FINESSE.

sites.name: Meteor (Barringer) Crater
sites.note: Best-preserved simple impact crater; Apollo and Artemis training.

sites.name: Lonar Crater
sites.note: One of very few impact craters in basalt – direct analog for lunar maria and Martian craters.

sites.name: Qaidam Basin – Dalangtan
sites.note: High-altitude hyperarid salt playas and yardangs; Tianwen-1 analog.

sites.name: Pilbara Craton
sites.note: 3.5 Ga stromatolites – biosignature analog for Jezero delta sampling.

sites.name: Pisgah lava field – Mojave
sites.note: Basalt flows over playa; radar and rover tests.

sites.name: Axel Heiberg Island springs
sites.note: Perennial cold saline springs through permafrost.

sites.name: Nördlinger Ries
sites.note: Complex impact crater; Apollo 14 and Artemis geology training.

sites.name: Dhofar desert (AMADEE-18)
sites.note: Austrian Space Forum Mars simulation; meteorite-rich hyperarid plains.

sites.name: Makhtesh Ramon (D-MARS)
sites.note: Erosion cirque; D-MARS and AMADEE-20 habitats.

sites.name: Dome C – Concordia Station
sites.note: ESA isolation analog; extreme cold, polar night, low pressure.

sites.name: Dallol – Danakil Depression
sites.note: Hyper-acid, hyper-saline hydrothermal field; limits of habitability for Mars.

sites.name: Dasht-e Lut (Kaluts)
sites.note: Hottest land surface on Earth (MODIS) and giant yardangs like Medusae Fossae.

sites.name: Salar de Uyuni
sites.note: Largest salt flat; high altitude, intense UV; chloride-deposit analog.

sites.name: Campo de Piedra Pómez – Puna
sites.note: Wind-sculpted ignimbrite at ~3,000 m; aeolian erosion like Martian yardangs.

sites.name: Salar de Pajonales
sites.note: Gypsum domes at 3,500 m with extreme UV; NASA SETI Institute astrobiology.

sites.name: Licancabur & Laguna Verde
sites.note: Highest lakes on Earth; analog for ancient Martian paleolakes.

sites.name: Arenal del Chimborazo
sites.note: Andesitic ash 'sand sea' at 4,300 m under equatorial sun – the point farthest from Earth's center; extreme UV, thin air, glacier ice reachable by road in 3 h from Quito.

sites.name: Cotopaxi ash plains (Limpiopungo)
sites.note: Fine volcanic ash and lahar deposits from 2015 eruption; glacier-capped volcano 1 h from Quito airport.

sites.name: Sierra Negra – Isabela, Galápagos
sites.note: Shield-volcano caldera with fresh pahoehoe and lava tubes – Arsia Mons / lunar skylight analog.

sites.name: Fernandina – Galápagos
sites.note: One of the most active, pristine basaltic shields on Earth; barren young flows.

sites.name: Tolbachik
sites.note: Scoria fields where Lunokhod rovers were tested in the 1970s.

sites.name: Namib Sand Sea
sites.note: Giant linear dunes; analog for Martian dune fields and aeolian mobility.

sites.name: Gilf Kebir – Western Desert
sites.note: Hyperarid plateau with crater fields and paleo-drainage seen by radar.

sites.name: Changtang Plateau
sites.note: ~5,000 m cold desert with permafrost and saline lakes; low pressure.

sites.name: Miller Range blue-ice fields
sites.note: High-latitude nunataks and blue ice: grazing sun, long shadows and ice – lunar south-pole lighting analog.

sites.name: Tenoumer Crater
sites.note: 1.9 km pristine impact crater in the hyperarid Sahara.

sites.name: Aorounga impact structure
sites.note: Eroded impact crater carved by wind into yardangs – textbook Mars landscape.

sites.name: Wolfe Creek Crater
sites.note: 880 m well-preserved crater in arid outback.

sites.name: Payún Matrú volcanic field
sites.note: Hundreds of cinder cones and long basaltic flows – lunar maria/Tharsis analog.

sites.name: Harrat Khaybar & Umm Jirsan lava tube
sites.note: Hyperarid basaltic field with 1.5 km lava tube – dry cave analog for Mars skylights.

sites.name: Undara lava tubes
sites.note: Very long, large-diameter tubes – scale analog for lunar lava tubes.

sites.name: Emi Koussi – Tibesti
sites.note: Shield volcano in the Sahara; long recognized morphologically similar to Elysium Mons.

sites.name: Rub' al Khali
sites.note: Largest continuous sand sea; Wabar impact glass; sabkha evaporites.
